correctness.rationale: By definition D²(X) is a graph with one vertex per 2-face and one edge per pair of complementary 2-sets whose union is a tetrahedral facet; three such edges per tetrahedron. The base ∂Δ4 has graph KG(5,2), connected with V10, E15 and β1=6. One facet stacking adds four new primal edges hence four double vertices; its removed tetrahedron contributes three deleted opposite-pair edges; its four new tetrahedra contribute 12 distinct incidence edges. The connected local bipartite replacement on 6 old plus 4 new double vertices links both endpoints of each deleted edge, preserving global connectivity. Thus after n−5 stackings V=4n−10, E=9n−30 and β1=E−V+1=5n−19; a connected finite graph is a wedge of that many circles. Independently formed the graph from listed tetrahedra and verified connectivity and counts for n=5..14; this bounded test supports, but does not replace, the all-stacking combinatorial argument.
